title.en: Write a system as AX = B

say.en: Write a system of equations as AX equals B. If A has an inverse, the whole system is solved in one step: X equals A to the power minus 1B. In this lesson: Write a system as AX equals B.
Decide consistency.
Solve using X equals A to the power minus 1B.

body.en: A system is consistent if it has a solution and inconsistent otherwise. Write it as $AX = B$. If $|A| \ne 0$, there is a unique solution $X = A^{-1}B$. If $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj}\,A)B \ne O$, there is no solution. If $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj}\,A)B = O$, the system may have infinitely many solutions or none.
body.kn: AX = B ಎಂದು ಬರೆಯಿರಿ. |A| ≠ 0 ಆದರೆ ಏಕೈಕ ಪರಿಹಾರ X = A⁻¹B. |A| = 0 ಮತ್ತು (adj A)B ≠ O ಆದರೆ ಪರಿಹಾರವಿಲ್ಲ (ಅಸಂಗತ).

points.en: |A| = 0, (adj A)B = O: infinitely many or none

narration.en: Write the system as A X equals B. If the determinant of A is not zero, there is exactly one solution, X equals A inverse B. If the determinant is zero, check adj A times B: if it is not zero, there is no solution.

say.en: Write the system as A X equals B. If the determinant of A is not zero, there is exactly one solution, X equals A inverse B. If the determinant is zero, check adj A times B: if it is not zero, there is no solution. |A| is not equal to 0: unique solution.
say.kn: AX equals B ಎಂದು ಬರೆಯಿರಿ. |A| is not equal to 0 ಆದರೆ ಏಕೈಕ ಪರಿಹಾರ X equals A to the power minus 1B. |A| = 0 ಮತ್ತು adj AB is not equal to O ಆದರೆ ಪರಿಹಾರವಿಲ್ಲ (ಅಸಂಗತ).

say.en: |A| = 0, adj AB is not equal to O: inconsistent.
|A| = 0, adj AB equals O: infinitely many or none.
The system x plus y equals 5 and x minus y equals 1 is two lines. They meet at one point, 3 2: one solution.
In matrix form A X equals B. The determinant of A is minus 2, not zero, so X is A inverse B.
If the determinant is zero, the lines are parallel or the same line. Parallel lines never meet: no solution.
If the determinant is zero and adj A times B is also zero, check further: here the lines coincide, so infinitely many solutions.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Solve 2x + 5y = 1, 3x + 2y = 7.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Solve 2x plus 5y equals 1, 3x plus 2y equals 7.
A = [2 5; 3 2], B = [1; 7], |A| = 4 minus 15 equals minus 11 is not equal to 0.
A to the power minus 1 equals (minus 1 over 11)[2 minus 5; minus 3 2].
X equals A to the power minus 1B equals (minus 1 over 11)[2 minus 35; minus 3 plus 14] = (minus 1 over 11)[-33; 11] = [3; minus 1].
So the answer is x equals 3, y equals minus 1.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Is the system x + 2y = 2, 2x + 4y = 3 consistent?

say.en: Let us solve this together. Is the system x plus 2y equals 2, 2x plus 4y equals 3 consistent?
adj A = [4 minus 2; minus 2 1]; adj AB = [8 minus 6; minus 4 plus 3] = [2; minus 1] is not equal to O.
So the answer is Inconsistent: no solution.
